title: History Is Path Dependent
concise_statement: Small random events can create massive long-term consequences through cascading effects.
detailed_explanation: Complex systems are highly sensitive to initial conditions. Minor decisions, accidents, or chance encounters can alter the trajectory of individuals, economies, markets, and societies in irreversible ways. Outcomes often appear inevitable in hindsight even though they were contingent on fragile chains of events.
implications: Respect randomness in success and failure.
Systems should be designed with resilience against unexpected shocks.

title: The World Is Fragile
concise_statement: Many important systems appear stable until a hidden vulnerability suddenly breaks them.
detailed_explanation: Systems often function normally while accumulating invisible fragilities beneath the surface. A small trigger can activate these vulnerabilities and cause disproportionate collapse or disruption. Stability is frequently an illusion created by the absence of stress.
implications: Do not assume past stability guarantees future safety.
Rare failures can dominate long-term outcomes.

title: Randomness Dominates Outcomes
concise_statement: Chance events influence outcomes far more than people intuitively recognize.
detailed_explanation: People prefer explanations based on skill, planning, or intent, but many major outcomes result from unpredictable randomness. Human psychology systematically underestimates luck because coherent narratives feel more satisfying than uncertainty.
implications: Use probabilistic rather than deterministic thinking.

title: Survival Often Depends on Tiny Decisions
concise_statement: Minor decisions made casually can determine life-altering outcomes.
detailed_explanation: In complex environments, seemingly trivial actions may interact with hidden risks to create irreversible consequences. Humans underestimate how sensitive systems can be to small behavioral changes.
implications: Risk management should focus on preventing irreversible mistakes.

title: Humans Learn the Wrong Lessons From Stability
concise_statement: Repeated survival without consequences encourages underestimation of risk.
detailed_explanation: When risky behavior does not immediately produce negative outcomes, people infer that the behavior is safe. This creates complacency and progressively increases exposure to hidden dangers until catastrophe occurs.
implications: Past success can reinforce dangerous habits.
Absence of failure is not proof of safety.
Repeated exposure can normalize extreme risk.

title: Hindsight Creates False Certainty
concise_statement: After events occur, humans exaggerate how predictable they were.
detailed_explanation: Once outcomes become known, people reconstruct narratives that make events appear inevitable. This masks the true uncertainty present before the event and leads to overconfidence in future forecasting ability.
implications: Study decision quality independently from outcomes.

title: Rare Events Dominate History
concise_statement: A small number of infrequent events often determine most long-term outcomes.
detailed_explanation: Most days are uneventful, but occasional extreme events disproportionately shape history, wealth, careers, and societies. Human intuition struggles with this because people expect outcomes to emerge from average conditions rather than extremes.
implications: Tail events matter more than averages.
Long-term planning requires resilience to shocks.

title: Parallel Universe Thinking
concise_statement: A robust strategy should work across many possible versions of the future, not just favorable ones.
detailed_explanation: Good decisions are those that succeed reliably under different conditions rather than relying on luck or a narrow set of circumstances. Robustness matters more than maximizing outcomes in ideal scenarios.
implications: Prefer durable systems over optimized fragile systems.
Evaluate strategies across multiple possible environments.

title: Complex Systems Produce Unpredictable Outcomes
concise_statement: In highly interconnected systems, outcomes emerge from nonlinear interactions that cannot be fully predicted.
detailed_explanation: Complex systems contain feedback loops, hidden dependencies, and interacting variables that create emergent behavior. Small changes can create disproportionate results, making precise forecasting unreliable.

title: Risk Compounds Invisibly
concise_statement: Small unmanaged risks can accumulate silently until they trigger catastrophic outcomes.
detailed_explanation: Risk accumulation is often gradual and difficult to observe in real time. Because systems appear stable during buildup phases, people underestimate how much vulnerability has compounded beneath the surface.
implications: Long periods without failure can hide growing danger.
